rule: Each skill primer practises at most 2 pending skills, rotating weekly
summary: Motor-learning evidence favours spreading practice across many short sessions over massing it (Cecilio-Fernandes 2018 systematic review of spacing RCTs, though in surgical skills, not sport). That supports short, frequent (2x/wk) primers rather than the exact count of 2 skills. Mixing skills (contextual interference) improves retention in the lab, but the effect was almost negligible in applied settings and in young participants (Czyz 2024 meta-analysis), so whether 1, 2 or 3 skills are interleaved matters little. Two skills in a 10-12 min window is a time-budget heuristic.

sources.note: Cecilio-Fernandes 2018 systematic review (11 RCTs, surgical trainees): spaced practice sessions beat massed practice for retention; best gap unclear
Czyz 2024, 54 studies: random/interleaved practice helps retention in the lab but is near-negligible in applied settings, so the number of skills interleaved matters little
